items.statement: A lean redesign of intake rework (a returned-referral queue and a fixed daily triage time) followed by the structured template will reduce returned referrals from 22 percent to 10 percent or less and the median time to triage from nine to five working days by June 2027, without raising template bypass above 25 percent.
items.rationale: Combines the intake-side redesign that halved lead time elsewhere with the completeness gains of required fields, and names bypass as a limit.
items.risks: Triage time may not move (claim c3); practice pushback may raise bypass.

items.statement: The template alone, without intake redesign, will reduce returned referrals but not triage time.
items.risks: Tests a change the intake does not intend to make alone.

items.statement: Allowing a documented exception when a rapid test is unavailable will prevent a rise in returned referrals from practices without kits.
items.rationale: Addresses the transition cost seen in the time series.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected as the aim of the redesign.
